en: You can observe Taal Volcano's main crater lake sitting on Volcano Island, which is entirely surrounded by the waters of Taal Lake in Batangas.
The Pasig River flows in two directions depending on the tide, visibly connecting Laguna de Bay and Manila Bay through Metro Manila.
The Banaue Rice Terraces are carved into the mountains of Ifugao, creating massive, visible stair-like steps that follow the slopes.
The Rafflesia flower found in Mount Kitanglad is the largest in the Philippines, featuring bright red petals that can reach a meter wide.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an underground river that flows directly into the sea, observable at its limestone cave mouth.
During the dry season, the water level of Laguna de Bay noticeably drops, visibly exposing muddy shorelines and sandbars around the lake.
The Tubbataha Reefs in the Sulu Sea contain vibrant coral formations that are clearly visible just below the ocean surface.
Mount Pinatubo's caldera now holds a bright green crater lake, visibly surrounded by steep, gray ash-covered cliffs in Zambales.
Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan City splits into two distinct waterfalls that drop simultaneously, creating a visible double cascade.
The white sand beaches of Boracay Island are made of finely crushed coral, giving the shoreline a bright appearance under the sun.
The massive root systems of mangrove trees in the Pambuangue Mangrove Forest are visibly exposed above muddy water during low tide.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of cone-shaped limestone mounds that visibly turn brown during the dry season.
